topStories.headline: Neighborhood Groups Threaten Lawsuit Over Toxics as Safeway Tower Moves Toward Final Approval
topStories.dek: Opponents of the 848-unit Marina Safeway redevelopment have escalated their fight, warning city officials they will sue unless contamination testing is completed before the project receives its final green light.
topStories.body:
The long battle over the proposed redevelopment of the Marina Safeway entered a new and potentially decisive phase in mid-August, as neighborhood groups threatened litigation over what they say is an unresolved public-health gap at the 15 Marina Blvd. site. <cite index="38-8">In an Aug. 11 letter sent to the directors of the city's planning and public health departments, Stuart Gross, the attorney for several neighborhood groups opposing the project, warned that the groups would sue if the city allows the development to proceed through streamlined review without first fulfilling what he contends are its environmental obligations and public health safeguards.</cite>

The legal threat came just as planners delivered a decisive ruling in the developer's favor. <cite index="77-4,77-5">Marina District residents who were hoping the city would determine Align Real Estate's polarizing Safeway redevelopment plan doesn't qualify for California's Assembly Bill 2011 got a rude awakening: the San Francisco Planning Department declined to object to the 848-unit project's pursuit of approval under AB 2011, closing off a central line of attack from opponents who argued the Safeway site did not qualify for the 2022 state law allowing for expedited greenlighting.</cite>

The environmental dispute centers on documented contamination beneath the site. <cite index="72-2,72-3,72-4,72-5">Previous investigations have detected petroleum hydrocarbons and other contaminants beneath the site. State regulators have said the findings do not pose an immediate exposure risk while calling for additional testing and investigation before residential redevelopment proceeds.</cite> The State Department of Toxic Substances Control went further: <cite index="73-13">a DTSC unit chief indicated that results from sampling locations in the vicinity of the site yielded readings "about twice the commercial screening level, and ten times the residential screening level," leading her to note "I don't expect this property to qualify for streamlined approval."</cite>

<cite index="76-4">In a memo sent to Marina Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, Planning Director Sarah Dennis Phillips said the Marina Safeway project "satisfies the environmental site criteria outlined in AB2011," and stated that Align must still conduct a "preliminary endangerment assessment" per AB 2011, but added that this requirement "will be met later in the permitting and construction process" and is not a condition for approval.</cite> <cite index="72-7,72-8,72-9">Neighborhood groups have threatened to sue over the city's call to move ahead without first requiring additional testing, arguing that the environmental questions should be resolved before the project receives its final approval. The developer has said it has complied and plans to comply with all environmental investigation requirements under state law. The lawsuit could still advance.</cite>

topStories.headline: Supervisor Sherrill Holds Fleet Week Hearing After July 4 Transit Fiasco; City Promises 30% More Muni Capacity
topStories.dek: District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill convened a hearing this week to demand the city be ready for Fleet Week crowds after gridlock swamped the Marina waterfront on the Fourth of July.
topStories.body:
<cite index="101-1,101-2,101-3">A San Francisco supervisor held a hearing Thursday to make sure the city is prepared for expected massive crowds for Fleet Week. Supervisor Stephen Sherrill said San Francisco underestimated crowds at both a Fourth of July celebration and a Formula 1 demonstration, which triggered problems and gridlock in the city.</cite> The annual event runs Oct. 4–12, with its headline air show over San Francisco Bay on Oct. 9, 10, and 11.

<cite index="61-1,61-2,61-3">San Francisco Fleet Week 2026 runs October 4–12, with the headline air show over San Francisco Bay on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, October 9, 10, and 11. The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are confirmed to return as the headliners, performing their full demonstration above the Marina Green and the Golden Gate.</cite> <cite index="55-2,55-3,55-4,55-5">The Parade of Ships on Friday, Oct. 9 can be seen from the Golden Gate Bridge to the Bay Bridge, with the reviewing stand at the Marina Green. The San Francisco Fire Department will lead the parade with their fire boat shooting jets of water into the air to celebrate the Fleet's arrival.</cite>

The city is responding to Sherrill's pressure with concrete commitments. <cite index="101-4,101-5,101-6">The supervisor said the city is assuming larger crowds and planning 20% more porta potties and 30% more MTA service capacity. Sherrill called for real-time coordination to understand traffic impacts, and the city is also coordinating with rideshare and autonomous vehicle companies to manage where they can and can't drop off and pick up riders.</cite> <cite index="102-1">Taking lessons from the Fourth of July fiasco, the city's Municipal Transportation Agency has submitted geofencing requests — a temporary off-limits zone for autonomous vehicles run by companies like Waymo and Zoox — for segments of major thoroughfares, such as Van Ness Boulevard, the Embarcadero and Lombard Street, during some Fleet Week events.</cite>

<cite index="57-10">San Francisco Fleet Week is free to attend, though ticketed viewing areas for the air show are available through the event's official website.</cite> <cite index="61-7">Roads around the Marina close for the show and parking is very limited, so if you drive, pre-book a space and expect to walk in.</cite>

topStories.headline: Upper Fillmore Dining Wave: Korean Steakhouse and Thai Noodle Shop Join the Corridor's Busiest Restaurant Moment in Years
topStories.dek: Two more Michelin-pedigree restaurants are taking shape on Fillmore Street in Pacific Heights this fall, deepening a transformation of the corridor driven by tech investor Neil Mehta's buying spree.
topStories.body:
<cite index="107-1,107-2,107-3">The owners of Michelin-starred Korean restaurant SSAL are opening an upscale Korean barbecue restaurant in Pacific Heights. Owners Junsoo and Hyunyoung Bae will open Monami this fall at 2001 Fillmore St.</cite> <cite index="107-4,107-5,107-6">Junsoo Bae told the Chronicle that Monami will steer away from the all-you-can-eat format often seen at Korean barbecue restaurants — it will serve both an à-la-carte and tasting menu — and focus on premium cuts of Californian, Japanese and Korean beef. "We're looking for the highest quality beef people can enjoy," he said. Diners will be able to cook their own meat on tabletop grills that discreetly pull smoke through the bottom of the grill.</cite>

A second new restaurant is heading to the same two-block stretch. <cite index="111-3,111-4">Chef and restaurateur Pim Techamuanvivit (Kin Khao, Nari) is taking over the former Starbucks location at 2222 Fillmore Street. The new spot has a working title of Khao Soi Ya, suggesting a brick-and-mortar version of Techamuanvivit's popular pop-up centered on the Thai curry noodle soup khao soi.</cite>

Both projects are connected to the controversial Upper Fillmore Revitalization Project. <cite index="107-10,107-11,107-12">Monami's arrival is part of a broader shift in Pacific Heights. Tech investor Neil Mehta, who's behind the project, quietly purchased several properties along Fillmore Street in recent years, including 2001 Fillmore St. His plans sparked some backlash and fears that older businesses would be displaced — some did close, though the decades-old La Mediterranee restaurant negotiated a lease extension.</cite> <cite index="109-7">Among Mehta's purchases was also the historic Clay Theatre, which he has suggested he wants to reopen as a high-end arthouse cinema and lounge, modeled after New York's Metrograph.</cite>

events.title: Presidio 250th Anniversary Commemoration — Film Premiere at the Chapel
events.description: <cite index="45-3">On Thursday, September 17th, 2026, the Presidio marks the exact 250th anniversary of its founding with public showings of a new commemorative film at the Presidio Chapel at 1 p.m., 2 p.m., and 3 p.m.</cite> <cite index="50-3,50-4,50-5">The film, Documenting Anza by Bike, documents cyclist Luis Valle's journey retracing the Anza expedition route from Sonora, Mexico to the Presidio, completing the trip on March 28, 2026.</cite>

events.title: Access to Adventure Day at Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.location: Crissy Field Center, 603 Mason Street, Presidio
events.description: <cite index="116-4,116-5,116-6">A free, all-ages family fun day at Presidio Tunnel Tops on Saturday, September 19 from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., focused on inclusive recreation and after-school and summer programs available in San Francisco, with a chance to connect with families and staff from Support for Families and SF Recreation and Park's Therapeutic Recreation and Inclusion Services.</cite>

events.title: KAIYŌ Handroll Bar — Mid-September Opening
events.description: <cite index="21-1,21-2">KAIYŌ Handroll Bar, the newest concept from the team behind KAIYŌ Restaurant & Rooftop, is set to open in mid-September 2026 in Cow Hollow, introducing the city's first dedicated Nikkei handroll bar, blending Japanese technique with Peruvian flavors.</cite>

events.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026 — Air Show, Parade of Ships & Ship Tours
events.time: Various times; air show Oct. 9–11, noon–4:00 PM
events.location: Marina Green, Marina Boulevard, and SF Waterfront
events.description: <cite index="61-1,61-2,61-3,61-4">Fleet Week 2026 runs October 4–12, with the headline Blue Angels air show on October 9, 10, and 11 above the Marina Green and the Golden Gate. Watching from the public waterfront is free; reserved seats are available for purchase.</cite> <cite index="99-4,99-5">Events begin with free military band performances October 5–6, expanding to ship tours and neighborhood concerts throughout the week.</cite>

moreNews.headline: Mess Hall Opens at Presidio Tunnel Tops, Completing the Park's Four-Year Build-Out
moreNews.body: <cite index="96-1,96-2">The Mess Hall at the Presidio opened on August 15, 2026, at 201 Halleck Street, featuring three restaurant concepts — Breadwinner, Dayboat Seafood, and Boda — sharing a single kitchen.</cite> <cite index="92-5,92-6">The new 6,200-square-foot food hall sits inside a restored former U.S. Army building overlooking the Bay, with views of Alcatraz Island, the Golden Gate Bridge and the city skyline. Inside, the three food concepts are joined by a café serving Wrecking Ball Coffee, a full cocktail and beer bar, and a grab-and-go market.</cite> <cite index="94-3">The Mess Hall is the last piece of Presidio Tunnel Tops to fill in, arriving four years after the park itself opened.</cite>

moreNews.headline: Marina Beach: South Asian Natural Wine Bistro Still One of SF's Toughest Reservations Three Months In
moreNews.body: <cite index="4-1,4-2,4-3">Marina Beach opened in June 2026 in the Marina neighborhood, and three months later, tables are still hard to come by. A storefront on Buchanan Street that once sold Venezuelan tequeños is now home to one of San Francisco's toughest reservations, holding just four bar seats, a side dining room, and a two-person kitchen turning out South Asian small plates paired with natural wine.</cite> <cite index="4-5">The restaurant sits on the ground floor of a residential building at 3659 Buchanan Street, one block from Safeway.</cite>

moreNews.headline: West Harbor Second Dredging Scheduled for October as Sand Remains a Recurring Problem
moreNews.body: <cite index="64-1">According to SF Rec and Park, the spring 2026 dredging episode at the entrance to West Harbor was completed on June 28, 2026, and will be followed by another episode in October.</cite> The first round of dredging — a $1.16 million contract with Dutra Group — was necessitated after a large sandbar blocked the harbor entrance for months earlier this year, restricting access for boaters, emergency responders, and nonprofits. <cite index="64-9">SF Rec and Park believes the planned breakwater installation will eliminate the need to dredge the entrance to West Harbor for 10 to 12 years, though the SF Marina Harbor Association has expressed skepticism about that timeline.</cite>

restaurants.name: A16
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand–recognized Marina institution serving Neapolitan pizza from a wood-burning oven, regional pastas, and a James Beard Award–winning Southern Italian wine list.

restaurants.name: Lucca Delicatessen
restaurants.description: Family-owned Italian deli operating since 1929, serving hand-made ravioli, house-cured meats, and legendary Italian sandwiches on fresh-baked rolls.

restaurants.name: Greens Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco landmark vegetarian restaurant operating since 1979 under the auspices of the SF Zen Center, with sweeping bay views from its Fort Mason waterfront dining room.
restaurants.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg A, Fort Mason

restaurants.name: Morella
restaurants.description: The Marina's first Argentinian-Italian fusion restaurant, blending housemade pastas and sorrentinos with wood-smoked meats and empanadas in an eclectic, palm-filled dining room.

restaurants.name: Delarosa
restaurants.description: Bustling Chestnut Street spot beloved for Roman-style pizzas, craft cocktails, and a heated parklet ideal for communal all-day dining.

restaurants.name: Lobalita
restaurants.description: Walk-in cantina in the former Tipsy Pig space offering open-fire Mexican cooking, $14 cocktails, tostadas, guacamole, and a sprawling back patio; open Tuesday–Sunday from 4 p.m.

restaurants.name: Dragon Well
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Chinese restaurant on Chestnut Street since 1998, known for handmade potstickers, tea-smoked duck, and mahjong tables operating six nights a week.

restaurants.name: Viva Goa Indian Cuisine
restaurants.description: The city's only restaurant specializing in the coastal cuisine of Goa, with standout tandoori fish, prawn xacuti, and vindaloo on Lombard Street.

restaurants.name: Perry's on Union Street
restaurants.description: A Cow Hollow institution since 1969, Perry's serves classic American fare — Cobb salad, hamburgers, chops — beneath wood-paneled walls in its original blue-and-white checked-tablecloth setting.

restaurants.name: California Wine Merchant
restaurants.description: Marina wine destination since 1974 that pours 25–30 wines by the glass from small California producers and doubles as a retail shop with a regularly rotating list.

restaurants.name: Roaming Goat
restaurants.description: Intimate Cow Hollow wine bar featuring rare pours from Armenia and Georgia alongside elevated bar fare such as grilled halloumi with truffled honey.

restaurants.name: Horseshoe Tavern
restaurants.description: No-frills Marina watering hole known to regulars as 'The Shoe,' with cold beers, a jukebox, pool tables, and wall-to-wall TVs for sports viewing.

restaurants.name: Wilder
restaurants.description: Relaxed Cow Hollow neighborhood restaurant from the Proof Positive group, known for approachable New American dishes in a comfortable, unpretentious setting on Union Street.

restaurants.name: Little Original Joe's
restaurants.description: Lively Italian-American restaurant on Chestnut Street serving pizza, pasta, and parmigiana in a see-and-be-seen setting with leather booths and branded cocktails.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Parma
restaurants.description: One of the Marina's longest-standing restaurants on Steiner Street, serving hearty Southern Italian comfort food in a warm, family-run atmosphere for roughly 30 years.

restaurants.name: Ace Wasabi's Rock-N-Roll Sushi
restaurants.description: High-energy Marina sushi hotspot serving creative rolls alongside sake and Japanese-inspired cocktails, with a nightly happy hour from 5–6 p.m.

restaurants.name: SusieCakes
restaurants.description: Marina bakery specializing in from-scratch layer cakes, cupcakes, and cookies made with all-natural ingredients and European-style butter, with custom cakes available for special occasions.

hotels.name: Hotel Drisco Pacific Heights
hotels.description: An elegant, award-winning Pacific Heights boutique hotel in a restored 1903 Edwardian building, offering complimentary breakfast, evening wine service, and a free neighborhood car service.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: The only hotel within the Presidio National Park, housed in the restored Georgian Revival Pershing Hall with 22 rooms and suites, daily breakfast buffet, and evening wine and cheese receptions by a fire pit.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Restored historic Army officers' barracks within the Presidio offering sweeping views from the Golden Gate Bridge to Alcatraz, with complimentary breakfast and easy access to Presidio Tunnel Tops.

hotels.name: Hotel Del Sol
hotels.description: A retro 1950s motor lodge transformed into a colorful, playful boutique hotel in the Marina with a heated outdoor pool and complimentary continental breakfast in a sunny courtyard.

hotels.name: Pacific Heights Inn
hotels.description: Conveniently located between Cow Hollow and the Marina District, this inn offers free on-site parking and free Wi-Fi — rare amenities in San Francisco — making it practical for business and leisure travelers.

hotels.name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
hotels.description: Comfortable Lombard Street motel offering spacious rooms and suites in the heart of Cow Hollow, with easy access to Union Street dining and the Marina waterfront.

hotels.name: Infinity Hotel San Francisco, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
hotels.description: Contemporary Marina hotel in the Tapestry Collection by Hilton, offering stylish rooms, a fitness center, and convenient access to Chestnut Street restaurants and the Presidio.

hotels.name: Jackson Court San Francisco
hotels.description: A charming ten-room inn housed in a historic 1900 Pacific Heights townhouse, offering understated elegance and a quiet retreat steps from Fillmore Street shopping.

shops.name: Books Inc. in the Marina
shops.description: The Marina's full-service independent bookstore — part of the West's oldest independent bookselling company, founded in 1857 — with a strong children's section, author events, and curated staff picks.

shops.name: ei Home
shops.description: Chestnut Street boutique offering rare candles, fine fragrances, and thoughtfully curated gifts that are hard to find elsewhere in the city.

shops.name: San Francisco Optics by Alexander Daas
shops.description: Family-owned eyewear shop on Chestnut Street for over 45 years, offering a curated selection of luxury frames and prescription lenses.

shops.name: Cost Plus World Market
shops.type: Home goods and specialty foods store
shops.description: Large-format retailer on Marina Boulevard offering imported foods, wines, furniture, and eclectic home décor from around the world, a Marina neighborhood fixture for decades.

shops.name: Benefit Cosmetics (Union Street flagship)
shops.description: The original home of the San Francisco-born cosmetics brand, offering its full line alongside brow bar services in an intimate Union Street boutique.

shops.name: Plumpjack Wine & Spirits
shops.description: Well-stocked Cow Hollow wine shop connected to the PlumpJack Group, known for a smart selection of California wines, spirits, and knowledgeable staff.

shops.name: Fraîche
shops.description: Chestnut Street provisions shop specializing in artisan cheeses, charcuterie, imported pantry goods, and prepared foods for picnics and entertaining.

shops.name: Past Perfect Vintage
shops.description: Sprawling Union Street warehouse stocked with vintage and antique furniture, lighting, and home accessories from multiple dealers under one roof.

shops.name: Fillmore Strasse
shops.description: Upper Fillmore boutique carrying a well-edited selection of contemporary European clothing and accessories for women, anchoring the street's reputation as a shopping destination.

shops.name: Marin Country Mart – Starbucks / Crissy Field area
shops.description: The Crissy Field / Marina waterfront area anchored by healthy take-out options and small specialty grocers serving the cycling, hiking, and jogging community along the bay.

artEntertainment.name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture
artEntertainment.description: National Historic Landmark waterfront campus housing approximately 30 nonprofit arts organizations, theaters, galleries, and event spaces, with 1.5 million visitors annually.

artEntertainment.name: Palace of Fine Arts
artEntertainment.description: Bernard Maybeck's Greco-Roman rotunda and colonnaded lagoon — the last surviving structure from the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition — serves as a beloved public monument and private event space open daily.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Beautifully restored 600-seat theater within the Presidio presenting live music, dance, theatre, film, and special events in a historic park setting.

artEntertainment.name: ArtSeed at Tides Converge in The Presidio
artEntertainment.description: Presidio-based arts education nonprofit whose China Brotsky and Seed Galleries host year-round open-call exhibitions and mentorship programs open to the public on weekdays.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Engaging museum in the Presidio exploring the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with interactive galleries, archival film, and rotating special exhibitions in a stunning waterfront setting.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club / Heritage Gallery
artEntertainment.description: The oldest standing structure in San Francisco, the restored Officers' Club hosts free public exhibitions on the Presidio's multi-layered history, including Ramaytush Ohlone heritage and military eras.

artEntertainment.name: SFMOMA Artists Gallery at Fort Mason
artEntertainment.description: Nonprofit gallery at Fort Mason presenting and selling works by Bay Area artists, supporting SFMOMA's education and community programs.
artEntertainment.address: Bldg A, Fort Mason Center, Marina Blvd

artEntertainment.name: Gathering for Justice Gallery / Magic Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Fort Mason-based theater company known for world premieres and bold new American plays, operating since 1967 with an intimate mainstage and a second performance space.

gymsRecreation.name: Karma Yoga SF
gymsRecreation.description: Pacific Heights yoga studio at 2219 Filbert Street offering hot power yoga, karmic flow, and hot HIIT flow classes in a dedicated heated space.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – The Marina
gymsRecreation.description: Marina location of the national CorePower Yoga chain, offering heated power yoga, yoga sculpt, and restorative classes with a flexible drop-in and membership model.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot 8 Yoga – Marina
gymsRecreation.description: Marina outpost of the Hot 8 Yoga chain offering a full range of heated yoga classes from Power 1 to Yoga Sculpt, Yoga Barre, and restorative Yin in a consistently clean, spa-like environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Alta Plaza Park
gymsRecreation.description: Tiered hilltop park in Pacific Heights with playground equipment, tennis courts, and panoramic views stretching from the bay to the hills, popular with families and dog owners.
